harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired `/srv/legacy2/batch-exclusive-lock/bin/reconcile`. Concurrent runs are now serialized with kernel-managed `flock`; contention returns exit 75 with a clear message. Existing ledger data survived, pending IDs occur exactly once, interruption recovery works, and the repair persisted across node1’s reboot.
actions_performed: Added a nonblocking whole-job lock using the installed util-linux `flock`.
Changed batch processing to safe line-by-line reads with exact fixed-string ledger checks.
Verified concurrent execution, interruption recovery, and idempotent reruns.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its changed boot identity, unchanged OS/kernel, script persistence, locking behavior, and ledger integrity.

evidence.requirement: Only one invocation processes pending.tsv at a time, with a clear contention result
evidence.summary: Concurrent runs returned 0 and 75; the rejected invocation reported `reconcile: another invocation already owns the job`. The same behavior worked after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Each pending batch ID reaches ledger.tsv exactly once and existing entries are preserved
evidence.summary: Original B100 was preserved. B101 and B102 were added once each and remained singletons after idempotent reruns and reboot.

evidence.requirement: An interrupted invocation does not permanently block later work
evidence.summary: A test invocation was interrupted with exit 143; the subsequent run completed successfully and every test ledger ID occurred exactly once.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Alpine Linux 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were identical before and after restart.

Captured healthy baseline under boot ID 2151a9b2-6404-449a-a09a-7041d90c64d2, received reboot acknowledgement, observed new boot ID 3f68f4cf-0c18-43c8-81a7-4ae6fc98a64b, and verified the persistent script, locking behavior, and exact-once ledger state.
